Messages.Author: Chris Shorb & Tammy Martin
Messages.Body:
I am both an avid V:TES player and a game store owner. I
promote Jyhad here in the store with a regular play night.
Recently, some of our players have started to fade away,
just attrition I guess. So that means we need new players
right? So I began gearing up for a demo, when I realized,
if I do hook a new player, there is one glaring thing in
their way to enjoyment and competetiveness (perhaps the same
thing) in this game.

A lack of cards.

I can still get Jyhad/V:TES for relatively cheap or through
standard distribution channels. And Jyhad is a good set.
But let's be honest, Ancient Hearts and the Sabbat have the
cards that everyone wants multiples of, no matter what
discipline or clan they are playing. And both those sets
are gone, baby gone. Mark Korshavn never seems to get back
in some of the more popular Sabbat cards (Entombment, Hungry
Coyote to name two), or if he does they are gone
immediately, and with the dearth of Sabbat unopened packs,
he never will.

So my demo scenario will look like this. New player(s) come
and learn how to play in the demo environment - everyone
playing pretty much the beginner decks that someone has been
posting here or that one finds on the Madness Network site.
We even give each player 500 common Jyhad cards and extra
vamps (I got them, no worries). They come back the next
week and we play open format, wherein many of us are trying
to make tournament decks work. New player gets pummeled by a
bunch of rare or even common Sabbat/Ancient Hearts cards.
Thinks either "well, that was no fun, I quit" or "that was
interesting, how can I compete". The first player might be
lost to us, but the second is worth saving. However, the
new player can no longer compete with those of us who have
been in the game for a long time. _Can not compete_. Not
unless they are a masochist, or somehow manage to make some
killer trades with the older generation Methuselahs, or are
content to play the same deck over and over (and most likely
lose).

At one time a great selling point of this game was that it
was inexpensive. Some of it still is, just not the good
stuff.

So Wizards - as a store owner, I pledge that if you reprint
the Sabbat, I will personally for the store buy 100 boxes on
the initial order. And if you reprint Ancient Hearts, I
will personally buy 50 boxes on initial order. And if you
print a new set, I will buy 200 boxes on intial order
(that's about $10,000 wholesale for those scoring at home).
I like to put my money where my mouth is...

Chris

--
Chris Shorb, Monger of stuff
Tammy Martin, Queen of the Eastern Marches, and damn good
mom

Messages.Author: Derek S. Ray
Messages.Body:
On 6 Oct 1999 20:44:30 GMT, phil...@eel.ENGR.ORST.EDU (Jasper
Phillips) wrote:

>[Snip more stuff saying AH and Sabbat have the power cards]
>
>Huh. I haven't found that to be the case at all. Granted, some
>of the later vampires are more powerfull, but those aren't that
>hard to come by, and you don't really need multiples. I definitely
>haven't found that people with older cards can't compete, just
>that they can't play as wide of a variety of decks.

Without Apportation and the Sabbat vamps, the Tremere are
significantly weaker than they already are. Good luck getting 12
Immortal Grapples by purchasing only Jyhad/V:TES boxes - the
uncommon-ness of it in Sabbat was necessary. Tribute to the Master
made "minion horde" decks even more fearsome. The Sabbat and AH
vampires are in very short supply - and THOSE can differentiate
between identical decks all on their own (Jimmy Dunn and Hugo being
big examples - Jacob Bragg being an excellent fill-in for Dr. Dre that
won't contest - Mitchell, Headhunter - and those are just the potence
combat guys.) Pursuit was an excellent Celerity card. Side Strike is
great too if your deck likes to dodge (Acrobatics is nice but *does*
cost blood - having an alternative is great). Pushing the Limit is an
excellent way to make Potence a "backup" discipline without burning
too many card slots - think Nosferatu Bruise/Vote. Forgotten
Labyrinth was awesome - the card Obfuscate *really* needed, and not
abusable by the Malkavian Dominate guys. The Fortitude cards provide
excellent variety in damage-prevent: you can choose what flavor to put
in your deck as necessary, as opposed to "Hm, Skin of Rock or Skin of
Steel?" How many *additional* Presence bleed cards did we get? Not
to mention Awe. Hm. Political Stranglehold is a brutal card for a
big-vampire vote deck late in the game. Guard Dogs is a card no
Animalism-untap deck should be without. Precognition for Auspex is a
GREAT include - Auspex got a LOT of cards in the Sabbat, actually, but
a lot of them were also rare. Dominate got Foreshadowing Destruction
in Ancient Hearts - OW!

You know, I can't think of any Protean cards that really make my
weasel tingle. Quick Meld is nice for a Form of Mist deck, though -
those pesky IGer's have a long way to go to catch up to *two*
maneuvers.

>I'm curious, which specific later edition cards are the newbies
>missing that they _need_ to compete?

...see above. There are an awful lot that when used in quantity
really set a deck one notch above a similar Jyhad/V:TES/DS deck. It's
not that a newbie can't make an effective deck, it's that without
picking from a VERY small list of types, he can't make one as good as
the decks he sees everyone else play - and will sit there going "damn,
I wish I had some of those cards", getting more and more frustrated
'til he finally quits. (some people are instant-gratification types -
they quit immediately.) Sure, he can play a Ventrue Law Firm deck and
that will be effective. And just as surely, someone will lug out the
Ventrue Antitribu vote-smacking deck the next week and pummel them
with a stick. The Sabbat vamps/cards made a lot of new strategies
viable - to me, making a difficult idea work in a deck is a lot of the
fun of the game. If it wasn't, I'd just play Presence
misdirect-bleed.

I would love to see them reprint Sabbat - I would buy a couple more
boxes immediately. AH as well, but because I do have a couple Sabbat
boxes I don't feel the lack as much. I would be delighted to have
Alacrity, Dreams of the Sphincter, Tomb of Ramses, and a few of the
other wack masters - oh, and those last two cards are effectively
GONE. I will never own one of either without a reprint: NOBODY is
selling unless they are quitting the game, which is a Bad Thing in
itself.

-- Derek

Messages.Body:
On Thu, 7 Oct 1999, Derek S. Ray wrote:

> Without Apportation and the Sabbat vamps, the Tremere are
> significantly weaker than they already are. Good luck getting 12
> Immortal Grapples by purchasing only Jyhad/V:TES boxes

I have about 16 Jyhad IGs, actually. When boxes are cheap, you can afford
to buy lots. I've spent less money on Jyhad boxes than I have on Sabbat,
and I have more Jyahd IGs than Sabbat ones.

> The Sabbat and AH vampires are in very short supply - and THOSE can
> differentiate between identical decks all on their own (Jimmy Dunn and
> Hugo being big examples - Jacob Bragg being an excellent fill-in for Dr.
> Dre that won't contest - Mitchell, Headhunter - and those are just the
> potence combat guys.)

They are? You can buy them for $.25 or $.50 a pop from any of the online
traders.

> Pursuit was an excellent Celerity card. Side Strike is
> great too if your deck likes to dodge (Acrobatics is nice but *does*
> cost blood - having an alternative is great). Pushing the Limit is an
> excellent way to make Potence a "backup" discipline without burning
> too many card slots - think Nosferatu Bruise/Vote. Forgotten
> Labyrinth was awesome - the card Obfuscate *really* needed, and not
> abusable by the Malkavian Dominate guys. The Fortitude cards provide
> excellent variety in damage-prevent: you can choose what flavor to put
> in your deck as necessary, as opposed to "Hm, Skin of Rock or Skin of
> Steel?" How many *additional* Presence bleed cards did we get? Not
> to mention Awe. Hm. Political Stranglehold is a brutal card for a
> big-vampire vote deck late in the game. Guard Dogs is a card no
> Animalism-untap deck should be without. Precognition for Auspex is a
> GREAT include - Auspex got a LOT of cards in the Sabbat, actually, but
> a lot of them were also rare. Dominate got Foreshadowing Destruction
> in Ancient Hearts - OW!

Sure, AH and Sabbat have some good cards -- I don't think that most of
these examples are inherently _better_ than their Jyhad equivalents,
however. I will concede that Apportation is more useful in most instances
than Movement of the Mind, but I think that of the other common combat
cards you mention, none are really 'game-breaking' in that they make the
Jyhad set pointless to play.

Your argument seems to be that certain expansions make certain decks
possible to play, and without them you can't play that deck. Well, yeah.
It's almost a tautology: Without Ancient Hearts, which is the only
expansion with Assamites, you can't play an Assamite deck.

Without Jyhad, you couldn't play any Camarilla decks. Without Dark
Sovereigns you couldn't play Giovanni or Ravnos (except some really weird
decks which consist of four copies of each of the three Ravnos cards in
AH, I suppose).

So you're basically saying that WotC should keep all expansions in print
forever? Sorry, me bucko, but that's not the way it works. Look at M:tG --
the Legends and Dark sets were massively popular, and massively
underprinted... but rather than putting those sets back into print, they
rolled some of the cards into the Chronicles set or later Unlimited
editions.

I think that you'd get better mileage asking WotC to publish a second
Unlimited (V:tES) edition, incorporating some of the cards from later
expansions (e.g. Apportation) than you will by asking them to go against
the business model they've worked out for the only truly successful CCG of
all time.

My two pence.

Fish.

Is Pursuit better than Flash? No, just different. But Flash is Jyhad
CEL's only maneuver card - meaning you have to pack a bunch in to be
sure of your maneuvers, risking having too many when you don't need
them. With the option to include Flash *and* Pursuit, you can cut
down on the Flash, since I know there are a number of times when I
only need to hit the guy one more time, not two, and I don't have to
spend a blood for a Blur and an unnecessary third strike. A deck that
goes from only Flash/Blur to Flash/Pursuit/Blur increases its
effectiveness significantly. This was more what I meant by listing
all the cards above - not that they made their predecessors OBSOLETE,
or that they broke the game, but that they start to be more than just
"nice to have".

>Your argument seems to be that certain expansions make certain decks
>possible to play, and without them you can't play that deck. Well, yeah.

No, it's that the expansions make existing deck designs significantly
more EFFECTIVE, and make new deck designs POSSIBLE. The first part is
the real problem.

[snip obvious about assamite decks w/o AH and ravnos w/o DS]

>So you're basically saying that WotC should keep all expansions in print
>forever? Sorry, me bucko, but that's not the way it works. Look at M:tG --
>the Legends and Dark sets were massively popular, and massively
>underprinted... but rather than putting those sets back into print, they
>rolled some of the cards into the Chronicles set or later Unlimited
>editions.

No, I'm not actually saying that - don't put words into my mouth ;)
No company can afford to do that. But since card rarity was not
supposed to be an issue with Jyhad/V:TES, it does not "break the game"
to reprint a set, unlike all those Magic players who would lose it if
you reprinted their rare cards they spent hundreds of dollars on each.
I think the most expensive card Korshavn sells is Protected Racehorses
at $10 - a V:TES ultra-rare. Reprinting the Sabbat or AH when a
sudden demand arises wouldn't hurt the game or WOTC that much - and
would provide us a chance to get a number of new players playing the
game, since we can point and say "Yeah, the Sabbat is expensive, but
at least you can GET the cards"... as opposed to "Yeah, these are
out-of-print" which REALLY turns people off.

>I think that you'd get better mileage asking WotC to publish a second
>Unlimited (V:tES) edition, incorporating some of the cards from later
>expansions (e.g. Apportation) than you will by asking them to go against
>the business model they've worked out for the only truly successful CCG of
>all time.

The model for Magic is "Make money, make more money, continue making
money, and don't yank on that hook in the gamers' mouths TOO hard or
they'll notice we're just making money." Game balance doesn't appear
to have been an issue (I believe they followed your suggestion above
and rolled Black Lotus or an equivalent power-rare into newer sets -
players freaked because of the rarity problem. I only know what I've
heard from friends unfortunately - i refused to play Magic long ago.)

The other problem is that I don't believe WotC is ever going to
publish another "new" set for Jyhad, after the current promised
expansion is done (and if THAT even gets done). It's obvious that
they don't see it at the top of their list, and the only way to
convince them otherwise is to provide them a low-effort way to show
that there ARE players out there now. About the only way to do that
is to reprint an existing set.

CEL and you are always going to want to use an additional strike? Do you have
mostly vamps with cel, and pressing will usually do the trick?

The Sabbat "variation" cards are handy, sure, but none of them are outright
better than their Jyhad counterpart, and you can always do just fine without
them.

Messages.Author: Madman2001
Messages.Body:
Folks:

I've been thinking about the fact that AH & Sabbat are OOP and
difficult to obtain to some extent. But, the fact is that V:TES IS a
trading card game, and people shouldn't dive into V:TES and expect to
be able to obtain any card they want (need?) immediately at a low price.

Frankly, I find V:TES cards just about as easy to obtain as Magic
cards. In fact, in terms of the difficulty and cost of putting
together a deck, V:TES wins hands down!

Let's look:

Cost of cards: I must say that it is cheaper to put together a V:TES
deck. First, you can buy boxes of Jyhad on eBay for $15 to $20 each.
Second, I have only seen one V:TES single priced over $10 (Tomb,
Korshavn) whereas the best Magic rares will often/usually cost that
much.

Obtaining cards: yes, it can be more difficult to obtain some V:TES
singles, primarily due to the thin market. However, I would expect
that one could obtain nearly any card given a bit of patience.

Cards phasing out: the fact is that V:TES decks don't become obsolete.
Competitive MtG decks must change 3 times a year, and once a year
about half your deck suddenly is no longer tournament-legal (Type II,
that is). It takes a huge investment to play Magic even at the local
gameshop level.

So, compared to the most successful trading card game around (ignoring
<ugh> Pokemon), it is actually easier and cheaper to create and
maintain a V:TES deck.

Yes, the lack of boxes of Sabbat can adversely affect the Draft/Sealed
environment, but still . . .

My $0.02.



I hate to say it, but Potomac and Edge-man and online card
discounters, while great for the end users such as your(our)selves,
carry no weight with WotC. When you have an established base of
2000-3000 shops selling at full retail, each buying 2-200 boxes of
WotC's new Magic product, that is Wotc's true customer base. And we
get that stuff through distributors. Also, I am not speaking
specifically of Jyhad/V:TES. I mean specifically Sabbat and AH.

This is an open invite to all who say "we don't need to have either
more expansions, or shouldn't reprint any of the two better sets (AH &
SAB)". Please make as many Jyhad/V:TES/DH *only* decks that you can
and only play them for two months, and then tell us a) how many games
you won b) how much fun you honestly had. And then post back to this
NG. Don't reply to this and say "Oh I have an all Jyhad deck that
kicks butt!" No doubt you do. But wouldn't you be really bored of
that if you played that _every_ time you played V:TES? And your
winning percentage would most certainly go down as people realized, oh
he's playing that Drawing out the Beast deck again, for the third time
tonight and the tenth time this month.

What I am talking about is enticing people to learn this very
complicated yet incredibly rewarding game. Learning a new game is
tough, and there are lots of barriers. Among those barriers are
finding other players, learning the rules, being interested in the
game, and accessibility to the game. Jyhad is very deficient in the
first and second (few players, extensive errata), but the third,
holding player's interest can be very high. If the fourth is also
high, accesibility, then we have a recipe for sucess.

> And Jyhad is a good set.
> >But let's be honest, Ancient Hearts and the Sabbat have the
> >cards that everyone wants multiples of, no matter what
> >discipline or clan they are playing. And both those sets
> >are gone, baby gone. Mark Korshavn never seems to get back
> >in some of the more popular Sabbat cards (Entombment, Hungry
> >Coyote to name two), or if he does they are gone
> >immediately, and with the dearth of Sabbat unopened packs,
> >he never will.
>

> [Snip more stuff saying AH and Sabbat have the power cards]
>
> Huh. I haven't found that to be the case at all. Granted, some
> of the later vampires are more powerfull, but those aren't that
> hard to come by, and you don't really need multiples. I definitely
> haven't found that people with older cards can't compete, just
> that they can't play as wide of a variety of decks.
>

> Are you playing with the official errata? If not, then I can
> certainly see how you'd have problems. However, the solution
> is easy -- play with the errata.
>
> Admitedly, most of the rare stuff I want is in the later sets
> (since they cost more), but they're generally funky cards that
> aren't really that great. I have plenty of effective decks that
> don't use any of the later cards, or that could easily swap in
> an older version.
>

> I'm curious, which specific later edition cards are the newbies
> missing that they _need_ to compete?
>
>

Besides the cards that Derek Ray mentioned, there are cards like
Direct Intervention, Recruitment, Tribute to the Master. None of
which are necessarily better or worse than other cards. But when
someone busts one out, the newbie will go neat! I want one. And then
can't get one.

And I want everyone to remember a few things. Not everyone playing
Jyhad have net access, or are interested enough to go shop for teh
stuff. In my playgroup, only 50% have net accesss, although all of
them have bought cards on teh net. I don't think most participate in
this forum however. And finally, if stores are not making money off
of the game, then often they don't want to support the game, in the
form of gaming space. So buying cards at the store, even if only a
pack or two every time, is a good way to support the game, get your
fix, and support your store.

I'm rambling at this point, so I'll sign off.

Thanks,

Chris

Messages.Body:
lor...@nospam.nineball.org (Derek S. Ray) writes:

>The model for Magic is "Make money, make more money, continue making
>money, and don't yank on that hook in the gamers' mouths TOO hard or
>they'll notice we're just making money." Game balance doesn't appear
>to have been an issue (I believe they followed your suggestion above
>and rolled Black Lotus or an equivalent power-rare into newer sets -
>players freaked because of the rarity problem. I only know what I've
>heard from friends unfortunately - i refused to play Magic long ago.)

Nope. They never did that. Certain people asked them to do it but
they refused to reprint any card they deemed "unbalanced". Black Lotus
is one such card.

What *did* happen is that they were reprinting a number of very *popular*
cards at one point (note the difference between "popular" and "overpowered"
or, as you call them "power-rare" cards) and a lot of people whined about
only that. This ultimately resulted in the creation of the "Reserved
List", which spelled out just exactly when, where, and how many expansion
cards might later be reprinted and guranteed that most rares never would
be (including a means of identifying which rares those were after a while).

Fred

This is a reply concidering the whole thread:

Of course it sucks that there are cards in short supply (e.g. Sabbat/AH)
but allthough some clans/disciplines are some what less playable, still
the basic set is the one to use. I find that most of my decks are just
spiced up by the later sets.
A couple of cards which are "the most powerfull" are:

*WWEF
*Minion Tap
*5th tradition
*2nd tradition
*GtU
etc.etc.etc.

It would be great to have acces to all cards on an equal basis, but
wouldn't it take away some of the 'Collectible' part?
This plus the fact that THE best thing about Jyhad/V:tes is the fact
that the most powerfull cards are the common cards and the unc. cards.
One thing I disliked about Sabbat was the fact that WotC deterred from
that path and made Rares that are so powerfull/unbalancing without mayor
drawbacks.
But this all means that even if you don't have acces to the Rares, you
still can trade for the commons/unc.'s. (or in my case give some of the
cards away for free to the newbies,.... don't I feel good about
myself <sigh>)
I feel that one of the problems today caused by the short supply is that
it pushes new players away from the game as they can't get the cards
they see others using without spending a lot of money on singles.
That's why I totally agree with the comment on sharing the cards with
newbies, or even trading them for less than usual. I mean: the more
players the merrier and come on: it's just a card game! It is about
interaction and a bunch of people getting together.
If you can get new players interested for this great game, share and
help them. Once WotC/Hasbro sees that there are more and more new
players getting into this game they might concider reprints and speed up
the release of new series as the game will become a beter investment for
them.

And yes I would buy at least two boxes of Sabbat if it would be
reprinted, but that's because I'm a V:tes Junkie. In reality I've
probably spend $1000 on V:tes in the last 4-5 years but buying the cards
did not enhance my fun, but simply sped up getting the cards I want, but
then without the interaction of trading.
(boxes in holland went for about ($125 per box)

Okay enough of my rambling,

LET THE JYHAD RAGE!!

greetings,

The Netherlands
